checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: AABB helpers + spatial-grid broadphase -> AABB character controller and trigger tracking -> raycast filter and docs/ADR -> full gates and delivery

impact_assessment.why: The physics layer still stops at individual ray/overlap queries, so games cannot efficiently find nearby bodies, move a character with gravity and collision, or react to trigger volumes; this is the next core roadmap item.
impact_assessment.benefits: A deterministic broadphase, a game-agnostic character mover and trigger enter/exit events give games reusable physics without genre rules; raycast filters let games restrict queries by key.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new keystone.broadphase, keystone.character and keystone.triggers public modules plus additive AABB helpers and RayHit/raycast; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none (caller-owned state); state: immutable bodies plus a mutable trigger tracker and caller-owned collider lists.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Unit tests first for cell boundaries, update/remove, wall/floor/jump resolution, trigger enter/exit and ray filtering; keep queries deterministic and the full 6/6 project gate.

[1/4] Plan an asset registry with stable IDs and content hashes, disk loaders for textures and OBJ meshes, dependency-aware records, and last-good hot reload; then wire the cube demo and docs/ADR

impact_assessment.why: The roadmap's next core system is assets: meshes, materials and textures are anonymous objects passed directly to nodes, so games cannot address, deduplicate, inspect or hot-reload them, and the demo cannot prove asset identity or refresh.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games get one registry for mesh/material/texture assets with stable IDs, content digests, duplicate detection, dependency tracking and a refresh report; PNG and OBJ files load through the same contract; a broken or missing file keeps the last good payload; no new dependencies.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new public keystone.assets module plus AssetRegistry/AssetRecord/ReloadReport exports and version 0.22.0, no report or web schema change; dependency: stdlib plus the existing geometry, texture, obj_loader and png modules only; concurrency: registry is caller-owned, refresh is synchronous and swaps one record per successful load, no background thread; state: no persisted files, source fingerprints live in memory, missing or broken files keep the last good payload
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for ID validation, kind inference, conflicts, digests, duplicates, dependencies, unchanged/reload/failure/missing/recovery refresh paths, custom loaders and wrong payloads; wire the demo through the registry; run the full 6/6 project gate and deterministic simulation before delivery

[1/4] Plan declarative material graphs: frozen node graph with color/float/checker/texture/mix/material nodes, topological evaluation with cycle detection, JSON serialization, registry texture resolution, tests, docs and ADR-028

impact_assessment.why: Materials are literal Material values, so reusable procedural surfaces, texture references and mixes must be rebuilt by hand in every game and cannot be serialized, inspected or compared by AI clients.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games and AI clients get an immutable, deterministic, JSON-serializable material graph that evaluates to one Material, resolves textures by name or AssetRegistry id, and needs no OpenGL or new dependency.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new public keystone.material_graph module plus MaterialGraph/MaterialGraphNode exports and version 0.23.0, no report or web schema change; dependency: stdlib plus the existing geometry, math3d and texture modules only; concurrency: pure evaluation with no shared state or background work; state: no persisted files, graphs are in-memory documents
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for constant color/float, checker textures, mix, cycle and bad-graph validation, deterministic evaluation, JSON round trips, texture-by-name resolution and registry resolution; full 6/6 project gate before delivery

[1/4] Plan dependency-free glTF 2.0 import: package with io, textures, materials, meshes, scene and loader modules; buffers, accessors, meshes, PBR materials, PNG textures, node/scene hierarchy, TRS and matrix transforms; tests, docs and ADR-029

impact_assessment.why: Keystone could load OBJ and PNG assets but had no path for modern glTF scenes, forcing asset conversion or hand-built meshes.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games and AI clients can import glTF 2.0 scenes, meshes, materials and textures without new dependencies or OpenGL, with optional AssetRegistry registration.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new public keystone.gltf package plus GltfImport/load_gltf exports and version 0.24.0, no report or web schema change; dependency: stdlib plus existing geometry, math3d, scene and texture modules only; concurrency: pure import with no shared state; state: no persisted files, inputs are read-only
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for triangle meshes, materials, translation, files, version validation, missing positions, embedded PNG textures, external buffers and registry registration; full 6/6 project gate before delivery

[1/4] Plan versioned scene snapshots and undo/redo history: History stack, scene_to_dict/scene_from_dict with asset references, tests, docs and ADR-030

impact_assessment.why: The engine had no way to save, restore or roll back a scene graph without OpenGL or a game-specific serializer.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games and AI clients can save, restore and roll back scene graphs without OpenGL, with asset references and bounded undo/redo.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new public keystone.history and keystone.scene_snapshot modules plus exports and version 0.25.0, no report or web schema change; dependency: stdlib plus existing scene, math3d and assets modules only; concurrency: pure in-memory state with no shared locks; state: snapshots are in memory, mesh and material payloads are referenced by asset id
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for undo/redo, capacity, deep copy, version validation, round trips and asset reattachment; full 6/6 project gate before delivery
